[34mInvestigated:[0m Read src/index.ts (unit constants, Unit type unions, parse regex and switch, format functions), the README unit section and examples, and src/parse.test.ts (Jest describe/it conventions). Confirmed the parse regex is case-insensitive and anchored, and that the switch's `satisfies never` check forces type and switch updates to stay in sync.

[33mLearned:[0m Unit parsing has three coupled parts: the regex unit alternation, the per-unit type unions that feed the exported StringValue type, and the exhaustive switch in parse. The millisecond branch returns the raw number, so microseconds must divide by 1000 to yield fractional milliseconds. The README documents casing and spacing rules, and those are enforced at the type level only through parseStrict.

[32mCompleted:[0m Parsing in src/index.ts now accepts the four microsecond aliases and divides by 1000, so `500us` gives 0.5 and `500US` works case-insensitively. A `Microseconds` type was added to the `Unit` union. The README unit list includes `Microseconds`, and a `ms('500us')   // 0.5` example was added near the top. A new test in src/parse.test.ts covers `500us`, `500 µs`, `1500 microseconds`, `1 microsecond`, `500US`, and `-500us`. The full Jest run passed with 168 of 168 tests and 100% coverage, and `tsc --noEmit` and `biome check src` were clean. The primary session reported that formatting is unchanged, so `ms(0.5)` still returns "0.5ms", and that nothing was committed.

[35mNext Steps:[0m The feature is implemented and verified. The session is idle, awaiting any further request.

[36mNotes:[0m The README example line was re-aligned after insertion, with a minor spacing tweak to the comment column. No new unit behavior was introduced beyond the requested aliases.
